question: How did FLEX droplet flames end with each diluent gas (nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium)?
claim: Most FLEX droplet flames ended in extinction with every diluent: 58 of 101 with nitrogen, 88 of 123 with nitrogen and carbon dioxide, and 40 of 50 with nitrogen and helium.
summary_student: In space, burning fuel droplets often went out before the fuel was used up. This happened in most tests, whether the air around them was diluted with nitrogen, carbon dioxide or helium.
summary_professional: FLEX (PSI-69) test end by ambient diluent: N2 101 tests, 58 extinction; N2+CO2 123 tests, 88 extinction; N2+He 50 tests, 40 extinction (n = 274). The other test ends recorded are disruption and completion.

params.sql: SELECT 'psi69_' || lower(replace(diluent, '+', '_')) || '_tests' AS name, count(*) AS value, 'tests' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.diluent')) AS source_columns FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-69' AND diluent IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table, diluent UNION ALL SELECT 'psi69_' || lower(replace(diluent, '+', '_')) || '_extinction' AS name, count(*) AS value, 'tests' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list_distinct(list_concat(list(json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.diluent')), list(json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.outcome')))) AS source_columns FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-69' AND diluent IS NOT NULL AND outcome = 'extinction' GROUP BY investigation, source_table, diluent ORDER BY name

method.formula: The values returned by the SQL query in params, one row per value, each with the source rows it used.

columns: CO initial ambient composition; mole fraction
He initial ambient composition; mole fraction
N initial ambient composition; mole fraction

assumptions: "Extinction" is the test end recorded in the FLEX table (column "Test end"); PSI does not define it further.
Tests are grouped by the diluent gases named in the FLEX table.
limitations: Counts outcomes only; oxygen level, pressure and droplet size also differ between tests and were not held equal.
Does not show that carbon dioxide or helium suppress fires better: the groups are not matched experiments.
Covers only FLEX droplet fuels (heptane and methanol), not solid materials.

chart.idea: Bars of FLEX tests and extinctions for each diluent gas.
